history.heading: Remote southern lands
paragraphs: The French Southern and Antarctic Lands (TAAF) include the Kerguelen Islands, the Crozet Islands, Amsterdam and Saint-Paul islands in the southern Indian Ocean, the Scattered Islands around Madagascar, and Adélie Land, France's claim in Antarctica.

Yves-Joseph de Kerguelen-Trémarec discovered the Kerguelen Islands in 1772, and other islands were found by French and other explorers in the 18th century. Sealers and whalers visited during the 19th century. France formally annexed the islands in the 1890s and created the TAAF as an overseas territory in 1955.

culture.heading: No permanent residents
paragraphs: There is no permanent population. Scientists, military personnel and support staff, typically a few hundred people at a time, staff research stations such as Port-aux-Français on Kerguelen and Dumont d'Urville in Adélie Land. Supply ship Marion Dufresne links the islands to Réunion.

politics.heading: French overseas territory
paragraphs: The territory is administered by a prefect based in Saint-Pierre, Réunion. France's claim to Adélie Land is frozen under the Antarctic Treaty. Madagascar claims the Scattered Islands, and Mauritius claims Tromelin. Much of the territory forms one of the world's largest nature reserves, the French Southern Lands National Nature Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

economy.heading: Science and fishing
paragraphs: Activity is limited to scientific research and regulated fishing, especially for Patagonian toothfish and rock lobster, which generates licence revenue. The islands host huge colonies of penguins, albatrosses and seals. The currency used is the euro.
